messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: Auth/token-validate error rate spike detected in production (svc=token-validate, env=prod) — page fired (PD#PD-8732) <https://pagerduty.example/PD-8732>
pagerduty-bot: Escalation: Primary on-call @jamal was paged; no ack in 2m, auto-escalating to @alex and @sre_lead
alex: acked — jumping in. I see increased 401s in frontend logs. Starting triage. :eyes:
jamal: oncall here, incoming handoff from pager — gonna run quick checks on signer and verifier pods
maria: customer support flagged spikes: some customers see upload API returning 401s and session refresh failing. Ticket count rising. Linking top request IDs.
li: past 5m from auth-proxy logs (filtered):
```
2026-03-14T15:22:10Z auth-proxy token_validate failed kid mismatch expected k_old got k_new request_id=abc123
2026-03-14T15:22:11Z token-signer signed token kid=k_new key_id=rot-2026-03-14-15:20
2026-03-14T15:22:12Z token-validator fetch_jwks status=200 cached_kid=k_old ttl_remaining=450
```
li: looks like token-signer started using a rotated KMS key (k_new) ~15m ago but validator services are still using cached JWKS with k_old — kid mismatch.
sre_lead: confirmed. JWKS cache TTL is set to 15m on most validators; rotation happened at 15:20 UTC. Some validator instances haven't refreshed yet.
sec_engineer: potentially customer-impacting auth failures. Priority: mitigate user 401s ASAP, then fix distribution of new key.
ops-bot: Suggested immediate mitigation: 1) Force JWKS cache invalidation; 2) Roll signer back to sign with previous key for 10m; 3) Increase JWKS refresh to 1m for validators during rollout.
jamal: executing cache invalidation script on validators (running across regions) — command: `for p in $(kubectl get pods -l app=token-validator -o name); do kubectl exec $p -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/clear_jwks_cache; done`
alex: running rollback flag on token-signer to dual-sign with old key for 10m. Patch applied to deployment token-signer-prod -> set env SIGNER_FALLBACK_KID=k_old
maria: tracking customer impact: preliminary estimate ~2.3% of token validations failed in last 10m across EU/US region; top affected endpoints: /upload, /session/refresh. Notifying critical account owners.
jamal: cache invalidation echoed success on 80% of validator pods; tails show new fetch succeeded and validator now recognizes k_new.
li: validators now logging accepted kid=k_new. Sample:
```
2026-03-14T15:23:45Z token-validator fetch_jwks status=200 cached_kid=k_new ttl=900
2026-03-14T15:23:46Z auth-proxy token_validate ok kid=k_new request_id=def456
```
alex: monitoring error rate — dropped from 12% down to 1.1% over 6m. PD incident still open until stable for 15m.
sre_lead: good work. Root cause note: KMS key rotation completed but cache propagation lag + no stagger/fallback on signer caused transient mismatch. Action items: make JWKS TTL refresh aggressive during rotations, add signer dual-signing grace period, instrument rotation canary.
sec_engineer: need post-incident runbook update. Add steps to notify validators to refresh immediately after key rotation; add healthcheck that compares signer active kid vs validator observed kids.
maria: created incident timeline and customer impact doc; notifying affected enterprises with rollback guidance and credits where applicable.
jamal: handing back to normal ops — I'm taking oncall out of pager escalation. @alex are you staying to watch the metric for the next 30m?
alex: yes will watch for 30m. If anything >2% error rate returns, re-open PD.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident PD-8732 acknowledged by alex. Escalation stopped.
ops-bot: Runbook checklist applied: cache invalidate -> rollback fallback -> verify logs -> monitor. Marking mitigation=complete, monitoring=true.
sre_lead: final notes: schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:30 UTC. Owner: jamal. Assign follow-ups: (1) lower JWKS TTL during rotations (maria), (2) implement signer dual-sign grace 10m (li), (3) add canary for key rotation (sec_engineer).
maria: added follow-ups to tracker: https://redwood.atlassian/INC-8732
alex: closing thread here once metrics stable. Great job team. :thumbsup:
